title: What is the Minimum Wage Rate in the UK and How Does It Compare to Australia?
description: Find out what the minimum wage rate in the UK is for 2026 and how it compares to Australia's National Minimum Wage. Learn to convert hourly rates to annual salary.
salarySummary: The UK National Living Wage from April 2026 is £12.71 per hour for workers aged 21 and over, while Australia's National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time Australian role, this typically assumes 38 hours per week. For example, $26.44 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $52,269.44 per year. This is a gross figure before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the UK minimum wage for 2026?
faqs.a: From April 2026, the UK National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over is £12.71 per hour. For 18 to 20 year olds it is £10.85 per hour, and for under 18s it is £8.00 per hour. Apprentices under 19 or in their first year also receive £8.00 per hour. These rates are set by the UK government and apply to most workers.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for the lack of paid leave entitlements. For example, Australia's National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading. This is paid on top of the base rate, not included in it.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia and the UK

If you have ever wondered **what is the minimum wage rate in the UK** and how it stacks up against Australia, you are not alone. Whether you are comparing job offers, planning a move, or simply curious, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is essential. This guide explains the formula, the key differences between the two countries, and what you need to know about tax, superannuation, and casual loading.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard calculation is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

In Australia, full-time ordinary hours are typically 38 per week. So for a rate of $26.44 per hour (the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026), the annual figure is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44

If you are paid fortnightly, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For the minimum wage, that is $1,004.90 per week, or $2,009.80 per fortnight.

This formula assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for comparison.

### What is the Minimum Wage Rate in the UK?

According to the UK government, the National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage rates change each April. From April 2026, the rates are:

- **21 and over**: £12.71 per hour
- **18 to 20**: £10.85 per hour
- **Under 18**: £8.00 per hour
- **Apprentice** (under 19 or in first year): £8.00 per hour

 provides the full table. For a 21-year-old working a standard 38-hour week, the annual equivalent would be:

£12.71 × 38 × 52 = £25,114.96

Note that the UK does not have a universal 38-hour week; actual hours vary by industry and contract. The UK also does not have a separate casual loading system like Australia.

### How Australia Compares

Australia’s National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the rate is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. confirms this.

At current exchange rates (approximately £1 = $1.95 AUD), the UK rate of £12.71 converts to about $24.78 AUD. So Australia’s minimum wage is slightly higher in dollar terms. However, cost of living differences and tax systems mean take-home pay can vary significantly.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

Many Australian employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum rate than the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each industry. Always check your specific award before relying on the national minimum.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees in Australia receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the minimum wage, that means $33.05 per hour. This loading is paid instead of paid leave entitlements. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains more.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a minimum wage earner, that adds an extra $6,272.33 per year to your retirement savings. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for details.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Australia uses a progressive tax system. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). For a full-time minimum wage earner ($52,269), the estimated tax and Medicare would be around $7,967, leaving a take-home pay of about $44,302 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

### Average Weekly Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026. That is more than double the minimum wage, reflecting the wide range of pay rates across industries. [average pay](/topics/average-pay) has more data.

### Summary

Whether you are asking **what is the minimum wage rate in the UK** or comparing it to Australia, the key is to use the same calculation method: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. Remember that Australia’s system includes casual loading, superannuation, and award rates that can lift pay above the minimum. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see your own figures.

For a quick estimate, try [the timesheet](/). It lets you enter your base hourly rate and add casual loading with a checkbox. Always check your specific award or agreement for the exact rate you should be paid.
